articleTitle: Ready for Takeoff
abstract: Dietrich is the chief operating officer at Terrafugia, a startup team of young engineers and private pilots in the Boston suburb of Woburn. In 2007, they began building the Transition, a "roadable aircraft" that transforms from a plane to a car and back again. When they set up Meteer's test flight they hoped to prove the concept and test the plane's stability and controllability ("rock solid," Meteer said). But they understood that how its performance was perceived would be as important as how it felt: If they could get people to buy into the idea now, it would be easier to sell them on the product down the line.

articleTitle: Gettin' Digi With It [Pipelining: Attractive Programs for Women]
abstract: Throughout the summer of 2009, Microsoft opened its campus offices around the world to bright and eager high school girls during the company's annual DigiGirlz High Tech Camps. For several days, girls were introduced to the latest innovations in the world of technology. DigiGirlz High Tech Camps' purpose is to dispel myths of what it means to have a career in the high-tech industry and give girls a chance to experience firsthand what it is like to develop cutting-edge technology.

articleTitle: Mothers and Daughters Make Sparks Fly [Pipelining: Attractive Programs for Women]
abstract: If there's one person whose passion is evident in motivating more girls nationwide to enter engineering fields, it's Celeste Baine. Award-winning author of books including Is There an Engineer Inside You: A Comprehensive Guide to Career Decisions in Engineering and Engineers Make a Difference: Motivating Students to Pursue An Engineering Education, Baine doesn't stop there when it comes to promoting engineering to students. She is one of the founders of The Mother/Daughter Technology Engineering Aptitude (TEA), a one-day event that lets middle school girls complete hands-on activities and interact with an engineering professional to learn about the engineering industry.

articleTitle: The Infusion of Creativity [Pipelining: Attractive Programs for Women]
abstract: This article examines the current state of engineering schools, particularly in the United States and abroad, by exploring how foreign and domestic institutional leaders can infuse their organizations with creativity, thereby producing innovative engineering students, globally. The article seeks ways to make the engineering discipline more attractive to students so that more young people will consider careers in math and science.

articleTitle: Becoming The Good Manager [Career Advisor: Experiences from the Real World]
abstract: Engineers and scientists have always excelled at learning and crafting technical proficiencies for their vocations, but there???s a new book on the shelves that urges professionals to improve their managerial skills. The Good Manager: A Guide for the Twenty-First Century Manager by Dean Gualco, while not industry specific, holds particular importance for engineers who are perhaps less known for their social and interpersonal abilities than for their academic and practical talents.

articleTitle: An Industrial Revolution [Amperes: Current Affairs from Around the World]
abstract: For the past four years Michal Judovits has been working for Ergo Consulting Group Ltd., an Israeli management consulting group. At age 27, she is a project manager with a team of ten people and a client list that includes both the largest bank and the largest insurance company in Israel. Yet, management consulting represents only a small part of an already impressive career???a career recognized by the Industrial Engineering Foundation when it recently awarded her the Instituto de Empresa (IE)-IEEE Women in Engineering Scholarship. Whether involved in the Israeli Defense Force (IDF), service work for nonprofits, or management consulting, Judovits has found ways to apply her interest and background in industrial engineering to a wide range of competitive fields.

articleTitle: Real-Time Innovative Thinking [WIE from Around the World]
abstract: To succeed and excel as an engineer, one has to be professional, keep yourself updated, and be open to new ideas.

articleTitle: Power and Responsibility
abstract: The paper presents the Humanitarian Technology Challenge (HTC) project. This group was created by IEEE members to address the problem of reliable electricity, data connectivity, and patient identification and healthcare records in developing countries.

articleTitle: Bolstering Biomend [Women to Watch]
abstract: A few years ago, Semahat Demir spoke to a group of graduate students at Brown University. In her remarks, she told them that there was “great potential for female role models, mentors, mentees, and peer mentors in biomedical engineering. Biomedical engineering is an ideal field for community building and peer mentoring.” When she looked through the data, she had found something fascinating: More women were getting biomedical engineering degrees than ever before—and at relatively high rates. There were also more tenured and tenure-track female professors than in any other engineering discipline. The message was hopeful.

articleTitle: Spaced Out [Women to Watch]
abstract: Hallie Gengl is not your typical college student. Yes, she might go to parties, hang out with her friends, or even cram the night before for an exam. But her accomplishments are what set her apart. Gengl, who is finishing up her sophomore year as a double major in earth and space exploration and meteorology/ climatology at Arizona State University in Tempe, is cofounder and vice president of Arizona State University???s (ASU) chapter of Students for the Exploration and Development of Space (SEDS-ASU), a nonprofit organization formed in January 2010 that encourages students to get involved in space exploration beyond regular classroom learning.

articleTitle: Eyes on the Prize [Women to Watch]
abstract: As codirector of research, senior scientist, and Ankeny Scholar of retinal molecular biology at the Schepens Eye Research Institute at Harvard University, in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and professor of ophthalmology and pathology at Harvard Medical School, Patricia D'Amore's groundbreaking research focuses on understanding the mechanism of vascular growth and development, with an emphasis on blood-vessel growth in the retina. She has written over 183 publications, some of which have appeared in journals such as Nature Medicine, the Journal of Clinical Investigation, and the Development and Journal of Cell Biology.

articleTitle: A Foundation of Consistency
abstract: On drugstore shelves across the country, there are bottles and tubes of foundation makeup by dozens of brands in dozens of shades. Buying foundation in a drugstore is tough. For one thing, the bottles and tubes are sealed, and there's no tester, meaning women can't try the foundation on their own skin. The same shade can look vastly different on various skin tones, and it always looks different when it's dry instead of wet. On top of that, there's no industry-wide consistency when it comes to naming foundation shades; one brand's "neutral beige" or "warm honey" can vary considerably from another's. And it can be extremely difficult to tell similar shades apart. Trying to pick your best color can be a minefield. There are lots of places to go wrong.But what if a woman could take a cell phone picture of her face, send it to a group of experts, and get back a text message recommending just the right shade of foundation? This is what Bhatti started to wonder after a large cosmetics company approached HP Labs. Bhatti likes customer-oriented innovation projects and has a particular interest in applied mobile imaging, the use of cameras to understand and solve problems. It seemed like a perfect fit.

articleTitle: A Volting Development
abstract: Marketing and flexibility help Hallberg grow Heliovolt. Hallberg's role is to serve as a bridge between the technical staff and customers and commercial partners. When the development teams need input on commercializing their designs, they can leverage Hallberg for customer feedback.

articleTitle: Guidance Counselors [Pipelining]
abstract: The Teacher In-Service Program (TISP) enables IEEE volunteers to share their technical expertise and demonstrate the application of engineering concepts to support the teaching and learning of science, mathematics, and technology disciplines.

articleTitle: Equal Opportunity Scams [The Good, the Bad, & the Ugly Engineering FACTS]
abstract: One of the greatest things the author enjoys about IEEE Women in Engineering (WIE) is the opportunity to collaborate with other organizations that are interested in helping women and young girls explore new career opportunities and realize their aspirations. It is sad that women have encountered such difficult struggles to develop successful careers in nontraditional fields, but it appears that scammers are equal opportunists and prey on anyone. These scam artists are counting on women's lack of confidence and insecurity to stay in business and out of jail.

articleTitle: The Love of Math [Women to Watch]
abstract: Kamakshi Sivaramakrishnan is at the forefront of engineering technology. As senior research scientist at AdMob Inc., one of the world???s largest mobile advertising networks with a wide range of products from mobile Web to in-application advertising and whose acquisition was recently announced by Google, Sivaramakrishnan drives the algorithmic machine learning techniques agenda for ad optimization and selection. As a scientist, she has developed cutting-edge algorithmic techniques for ad optimization and placement on mobile devices.

articleTitle: Meet the "Mother of the Internet" [Women to Watch]
abstract: Radia Joy Perlman is a software designer and network engineer specializing in network and security protocols for Sun Microsystems, now Oracle, a multinational vendor of computers, computer components, computer software, and information technology headquartered in Santa Clara, California. She holds more than 50 patents from Oracle alone. Dubbed the “Mother of the Internet,” she is most famous for her invention of the spanning-tree protocol???a link layer network protocol that ensures a loopfree topology for any bridged local area network (LAN)???that is fundamental to the operation of network bridges. She developed it while working for Digital Equipment Corporation (Digital), in Maynard, Massachusetts, a pioneering company in the computer industry, which merged with Hewlett-Packard and is now under the HP name.

Building a WiEM Network [Pipelining]
Electrical and Mechanical Engineering Education and Profession in Greece [Pipelining: Attractive Programs for Women]
abstract: Nowadays, the role of women in engineering becomes clearer, but unfortunately their underrepresentation in senior and leadership positions remains a worldwide phenomenon. The Faculty of Technology of Aristotle University of Thessaloniki (AUTh), Greece, carried out a study on the performance of female students during their education years and the first years of employment, aiming at improving their contribution to the engineering profession in the country.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Personality [WIE from Around the World]
Media Madness
abstract: I was cleaning out my office recently and came across the media storage that contained my Ph.D. thesis simulations. I remember how proud I was that I had successfully simulated over 2 million simulations for a digital system containing over 1 million transistors on a conventional single CPU computer. I tried my best to make the simulator portable and thought it would be an interesting project to see how it performed on a modern quad-core computer.

articleTitle: Do You Have What It Takes? Entrepreneurs face many fears and challenges [Letter from the editor]
abstract: What are you waiting for? You have great ideas and as an engineer, you know how to keep learning and adapting your skills to the marketplace. You have watched everyone around you become successful entrepreneurs, yet something is holding you back. Is it the fear of risk or, worse, the fear of failure? Many entrepreneurs don't start their first venture until they are older, have a home, and a family. Women tend to avert risky ventures and will sacrifice a potentially prosperous future for a failsafe path that seems more stable. What does it take to become an entrepreneur, and what is the mindset that one needs to finally take the leap and start a new venture?

articleTitle: Global Vision [WIE from Around the World]
abstract: Earlier this year, as we were kicking off 2010 around the world, new Women in Engineering Committee (WIE) Chair Irena Atov was thinking globally as well. The beginning of 2010 marked the start of her role as appointed chair and Atov brings an exciting list of goals and visions for WIE members and women worldwide to the position.

articleTitle: Strategic Leadership [WIE from Around the World]
GEOSS Who's Watching [Women to Watch]
abstract: It is often said that taking care of our planet is everyone's responsibility. We can each do something small, like turning off unnecessary lights or shortening showers, and the impact will be large. One woman who is calling on us all to do our part is Francoise Pearlman. Pearlman, now retired from a long career working with software, system of systems, and integration in the aerospace industry, is a volunteer with the IEEE Committee on Earth Observation (ICEO). She is also the primary point person for the group's outreach initiatives supporting the creation of a Global Earth Observation System of Systems (GEOSS) for Earth observation data.

IEEE Keywords: Global Earth Observation System of Systems

articleTitle: That Entrepreneurial Spirit Passion and diverse skills pave the way [Women to Watch]
abstract: An entrepreneur tends to bite off a little more than he can chew hoping he'll quickly learn how to chew it. —Roy Ash, cofounder of Litton Industries

articleTitle: A Segue to Bigger Ambitions: Programs break new ground across the globe [Pipelining: Attractive Programs for Women]
abstract: Though he's most recently known for his invention of the Segway Human Transporter device, Dean Kamen has a long history of working on really big challenges—everything from improving quality of life with portable medical devices to changing the culture of an entire nation with a robotics competition. The individual projects vary widely in focus, but the goal is always the same: “Find a serious problem and use technology to address it.”

articleTitle: Portrait of Pakistan [The Good, the Bad, & the Ugly: Engineering FACTS]
abstract: The IEEE recently welcomed a new Women in Engineering Affinity Group of students from Balochistan University, located in the Balochistan province of Pakistan. Given the country's history regarding the treatment of women, we wondered what it's like to be a female engineering student in Pakistan today. IEEE-Government College University Lahore (GCUL) Student Branch Chair Synnia Tanveer shares her experience. While customs and opportunities vary from rural to urban areas, it seems the future looks very promising for female engineers in Pakistan.

articleTitle: Flexing Their Muscles: Building a successful business partnership [Career Advisor: Experiences from the Real World]
abstract: What do you get when you pair a passionate and intelligent engineering professor at the University of Maryland with two ambitious and hard working recent engineering graduates? FlexEl.This company develops a novel, high-capacity, rechargeable thin film battery. IEEE Fellow Dr. Martin Peckerar, professor of microelectronic engineering at the University of Maryland's A. James Clark School of Engineering and the brains that helped launch the company, tells us how it all started.

articleTitle: International Talent, Global Solutions: Many influence the worldwide WIE movement [WIE from Around the World]
abstract: In 1942, at the age of 17 and just out of high school, Jack Sherman volunteered for war service. He enlisted because he wanted to join the U.S. Army Signal Corps. This would mean training at the Illinois Institute of Technology and the Metallurgical Laboratory at the University of Chicago. At the Met Lab, Arthur Compton was coordinating fission research. Enrico Fermi was developing the first nuclear reactor.

articleTitle: Reaching the APEX [Letter from the Editor]
abstract: Congratulations to IEEE Women in Engineering (WIE) and IEEE Women in Engineering Magazine! We are the proud recipients of two APEX awards for publication excellence and a Grand APEX award for the Nerd Girls video produced by IEEE.tv. We would also like to recognize the “WIE Ship the Chip” video, which documented our outreach visit with 100 young girls that was sponsored by our industry collaborator, the Microsoft Corporation. The video is one of the most popular videos viewed on IEEE.tv and remains a shining example that demonstrates the power of IEEE WIE collaborations with our members, educators, and industry partners.

articleTitle: Look Both Ways [Women to Watch]
abstract: In general, the growth of technology has made life easier. Instead of going to the store, you can buy almost anything you need online; it only takes one handheld device to access your phone, music, camera, calendar, and e-mail; and overall our capabilities as a society have improved.

IEEE Keywords: Global Earth Observation System of Systems

articleTitle: Only 20, Jain eyes teaching and mentoring [Women to Watch]
abstract: There are many medical students in the United States. In addition to the demanding pursuit of a specialty, some of those students spend their time trying to understand the business side of medicine; others who benefitted from mentorship work hard to help others follow in their footsteps. Very few manage to do both. Monica Jain is barely old enough to vote, but she is doing it all.

articleTitle: Reverse Bias [Career Advisor: Experiences from the Real World]
abstract: "Industry engineers are vocational." These are the words that introduced me to the longstanding battle of the biases between engineers in academia versus engineers in industry.

articleTitle: A STEM Launching Pad [WIE from Around the World]
abstract: IEEE Women In Engineering (WIE), South Africa Section commenced the Student Teacher and Researcher/Scientist (STAR) program for high schools from previously disadvantaged backgrounds within South Africa in August 2009. The theme of the STAR program in South Africa is “Launching the path into science, engineering and technology (SET) for the future.”

articleTitle: Smotrova Honored with 2009 Clementina Saduwa Award [WIE from Around the World]
Looking Forward, Looking Back [review of "The Bold and the Brave: A History of Women in Science and Engineering" (Frize, M.)]
abstract: Don't let the title of Monique Frize's new book, The Bold and the Brave: A History of Women in Science and Engineering, confuse you: the book looks forward into women's futures as much as it looks back. While the book spans 2,000 years of philosophers and thinkers with differing views on women's abilities and rights to education, “I wanted people to know that it's not a question of period or time,” says the author. “People don't think that women's inequality continues to be an issue and I wanted to demonstrate that it is still going on.”
